anti_overlap: OWN the provenance-attestation axis: whether a PRESENT, correctly-impressed envelope (has()-true, session-scoped) may be ENTERED AS A TRUE RECEIPT without a witnessed content-sealing behind it — the presence-of-record vs witnessed-content-of-container gap, cross-transaction envelope confusion, and the opened-refilled TOCTOU/staleness of the witness. The unit of analysis is the ENTRY DECISION (accept the impression as a true count vs refuse), and specifically the CUSTODY-OVER-TIME and WRONG-ACCOUNT dimensions of that decision.

Do NOT re-derive whether the two HASHERS cut the same byte-range datum or whether the parity vector exercises the real production code path / chunk boundary / real .mov container — that measurement-and-fit and test-oracle-fidelity axis belongs to the joinery-layout and golden-vector-fidelity lenses. Only touch the vector if a token-count is NEVER genuinely taken anywhere in the chain (an attestation gap), not to critique the vector's byte-range representativeness.

Do NOT re-run the assay-office's content-vs-mark framing as its own end in itself (touchstone/cupellation, mark-reuse/body-swap fraud on already-assayed metal) — that lens owns the 'a stamp is not an assay' and 'debased-body-swap' framing. This lens is distinct in its CUSTODY-CHAIN-OVER-TIME and MISFILED-UNDER-WRONG-ACCOUNT emphasis: a GENUINELY-verified envelope proving the WRONG transaction, and a once-witnessed seal that no longer witnesses the current interior — provenance and filing, not assay authority.

Do NOT audit the reconciliation loop as a pure Python control-flow / isinstance-guard / reason-code-selection exercise, nor the capability-Protocol structural-typing question as a type-system exercise — those statement-level and type-conformance axes belong to the fail-closed-control-flow and capability-security lenses. Only flag a loop shape or a Protocol-conformance gap where it manifests as ENTERING AN UNWITNESSED IMPRESSION AS A TRUE RECEIPT (a provenance forgery), not as a general truthiness edge or a general conformance-vs-compliance observation.
decision_lens: For every source_artifacts artifact_hash the manifest asks the node to accept, ask the storehouse accountant's question: is this exterior impression being entered into the account on proof that the SEAL WAS PRESSED OVER WITNESSED TOKENS FOR THIS TRANSACTION, or merely on the strength that AN ENVELOPE BEARING THIS IMPRESSION IS PRESENT IN THE ARCHIVE? A finding is severe when the node enters an impression as a true content-count without a witnessed sealing behind it: transport.has() answering only 'an envelope with these marks exists' (a presence-of-record) rather than 'these bytes were content-addressed at intake' (a witnessed sealing) — the has()-true-does-NOT-imply-verified-bytes gap, which turns entirely on whether EVERY conforming Transport, not just the one test-double whose send() happens to content-address, guarantees the sealing witness. Equally severe is CROSS-TRANSACTION BULLA CONFUSION: a genuine, correctly-content-verified raw sealed under session A being accepted as session B's lineage root — trace whether the (session_id, artifact_hash) key BINDS the envelope to this exact account at the point of reliance, whether session_id at that point is the node's own derived account-number or a device-declared one the sender controls (a sender who names his own account can file a valid envelope under any account he likes), and whether an artifact_hash alone (impression without account) could ever satisfy the gate. Severe too is the OPENED-AND-REFILLED envelope: a has() witnessed at receive time relied upon after the archive's state could change, alias, or be evicted-and-re-added between the sealing-witness and the landing side-effect — a time-of-check/time-of-use gap where the intact-looking seal no longer witnesses the current interior. And it is a P1 regression if the un-sealed direct-witness path (transport=None) does not settle on the EXACT prior trusted-on-the-scribe's-word posture — any new impression-check, guard, or default silently interposed on the legacy no-envelope receipt is a changed entry even if it 'looks equivalent,' because the contributor path and every current caller ride that direct-witness path. Rank strictly by whether an unwitnessed or misfiled impression can be ENTERED AS A TRUE RECEIPT (an unverified/foreign lineage root lands and redact/normalize proceeds on it) rather than REFUSED (fail-closed raise, nothing entered).
distance_rationale: Sealed-bulla token accounting is a pre-literate, non-Western, physical craft-bureaucracy of PROVENANCE-BY-CUSTODY — its whole subject is whether a sealed container's exterior claim may be trusted as a true statement of its interior, and its iron rule is that the seal certifies contents only if pressed over witnessed contents at intake, is bound to one transaction, and remains unopened. It shares no parent discipline with software, cryptography, type systems, index arithmetic, or accounting-by-count, and touches no AI-cliche domain (not biology/military/markets/information-theory/immunology). It is maximally distant from the five covered lenses: it is NOT assay (content-vs-mark authority) — a bulla can be genuinely, correctly sealed and STILL prove the wrong thing by being misfiled, the custody/wrong-account axis assay does not center; NOT joinery (datum/fit of two mating surfaces); NOT golden-vector test-oracle fidelity; NOT Python control-flow; NOT capability-type conformance. Yet it is a several-millennia-refined formalization of exactly the mk-lib posture the goal names: transport.has()-true is a present, correctly-impressed envelope, and the question is whether that presence WITNESSES content-verified bytes (seal pressed over tokens), whether the (session_id, artifact_hash) key BINDS the envelope to THIS account (not a misfiled valid envelope from another session), and whether the witness still holds at reliance (not opened-and-refilled) — the fail-closed refusal is the accountant declining to enter a receipt no witnessed sealing stands behind.
expected_isomorphisms: the exterior impression is a PROMISE about the interior, trustworthy only because the seal was pressed over the tokens at intake <-> transport.has(session_id, artifact_hash)==true must imply the bytes were content-addressed at intake; if the guarantee lives only in one Transport double's send() and not in the Transport CONTRACT every conformer honors, the impression was pressed over clay of unknown content.

to VERIFY you must BREAK the bulla and count the tokens; a matching impression on an intact envelope proves only that someone vouched for SOME contents <-> a content-hash of the actual bytes is the only proof of the substance; has() reporting presence is a register entry, and if NO layer in the chain ever content-counts the bytes, the reconciliation certifies clay not contents.

a GENUINE, correctly-impressed envelope from a different transaction, filed under the wrong account (right seal, right count, WRONG transaction) <-> a raw legitimately content-verified under session A accepted as session B's lineage root — the (session_id, artifact_hash) key must bind the envelope to THIS account at reliance, using the node's own account-number, not a device-declared session the sender controls.

an envelope OPENED after sealing and refilled, then re-closed, so the intact seal no longer witnesses the current interior <-> a has() witness taken at receive time relied upon after the archive could change/evict/re-add/alias the entry, or a long-lived Transport carrying a stale witness across sessions — time-of-check/time-of-use on the sealing witness.

an impression pressed over an EMPTY or wrong-token interior (a mark with no witnessed contents behind it) <-> a reconciliation-loop shape (null/empty-list/non-list/duplicate source_artifacts, or a lineage root claimed in an unreconciled field) that lets a manifest land with no genuinely-witnessed root — absence-of-envelope silently read as nothing-to-witness.

a quantity delivered and counted openly by the scribe's own hand needs no bulla ceremony and is entered on direct witness <-> the transport=None path (contributor + current callers) enters on the node's direct byte-witness with no impression-check interposed, and must remain that exact pre-diff trusted path byte-for-byte (additive-only).
focus: Whether the receive-time source_artifacts reconciliation obeys the sealed-envelope discipline: the impressed marks on the outside of a sealed accounting-envelope certify the contents ONLY if the seal was pressed over the actual tokens sealed inside AND the envelope has not since been opened, swapped, or re-used from another transaction. The lens treats each source_artifacts artifact_hash as an impressed exterior mark, the actual transferred raw bytes as the clay tokens sealed inside, transport.has(session_id, artifact_hash) as 'an envelope bearing this impression is present in the archive,' and the manifest landing as accepting the impression as a true count of the contents. It hunts for every path where the node accepts the exterior impression WITHOUT proof the seal was pressed over verified tokens (has()-true that never implied a content-witnessed sealing), where an envelope from a DIFFERENT transaction (a raw content-verified under another session_id) is accepted as this transaction's record (cross-session bulla confusion), where a stale/mutable/aliased archive lets an envelope be opened-and-refilled between the sealing witness and the reliance, and where the un-sealed path (transport=None) is not byte-for-byte the same trusted-on-the-scribe's-word posture it was before.
name: fd-bulla-sealed-envelope-token-reconciliation
persona: Apply the perspective of a Bronze-Age Mesopotamian temple-storehouse accountant working the sealed-bulla token system — the pre-literate physical provenance discipline that predates writing itself. In this craft-bureaucracy every incoming or outgoing quantity is recorded as small shaped clay TOKENS (a cone for a measure of grain, a sphere for a larger unit) sealed inside a hollow clay ENVELOPE (a bulla); the outside of the envelope is then IMPRESSED — cylinder-sealed with the responsible official's seal AND, later, marked with counting-signs that declare how many tokens of what kind lie within. The iron rule of the system: the exterior impression is a PROMISE about the sealed interior that is trustworthy ONLY because the seal was pressed at the moment the tokens went in, by the witnessing official, over that exact envelope. To VERIFY a bulla you must BREAK it and count the tokens — the impression alone is a claim, not a proof; a matching impression on an intact envelope means only 'someone with this seal once vouched for SOME contents,' never 'these specific contents are inside now.' The accountant knows the three classic frauds: (1) an envelope whose impression was pressed over an EMPTY or wrong-token interior (a mark with no witnessed contents behind it — the seal certifies the clay, not the count); (2) a GENUINE sealed bulla from a different transaction, correct in every impression, filed under the wrong account (right seal, right count, WRONG transaction — a valid envelope proving the wrong thing); (3) an envelope OPENED after sealing and refilled, then re-closed, so the intact-looking seal no longer witnesses the current interior. The accountant never enters a receipt into the account on the strength of a present, correctly-impressed envelope alone; entry requires that THIS envelope's seal was witnessed pressed over THESE tokens FOR THIS account, or that the tokens themselves were counted at intake. A quantity delivered and counted openly by the scribe's own hand, with no envelope claimed, is entered on the scribe's direct witness and needs no bulla ceremony — but the moment a delivery arrives already sealed, claiming an envelope vouches for it, that envelope must be shown to have been sealed over these tokens for this account, or the receipt is refused. A miscounted receipt entered as true is a false debit against the temple's stores — here, an unverified lineage root entered as content-witnessed is a false provenance against a contributor's privacy.
review_areas: Seal-pressed-over-witnessed-tokens rule (has() implies verified bytes): prove that transport.has(session_id, artifact_hash) returning true can ONLY be true because a content-witnessed sealing occurred — i.e. that the sealing-over-tokens guarantee lives in the Transport CONTRACT that every conforming envelope-keeper must honor, not merely in InMemoryTransport.send()'s incidental behavior of content-addressing on send. If a conforming Transport could record presence for a hash it never content-verified (an envelope impressed over empty clay), the gate enters an unwitnessed impression as a true count. This is the highest-value axis: the whole reconciliation's soundness rests on has()==witnessed-sealing, and the diff proves it only for the test double.

Cross-transaction bulla confusion (session-key binding at reliance): trace the (session_id, artifact_hash) key from the manifest's declared session down to the transport.has() call. Confirm the session_id used to scope the lookup is the account-number the NODE independently owns for this landing, not one the device declared and controls — if the sender names his own session_id, a valid envelope he legitimately sealed under one account can be filed under any account, defeating the wrong-session refusal the diff's own test asserts. Check that an artifact_hash can never satisfy the gate WITHOUT its session half (impression accepted without an account), and that two sessions cannot collide onto one archive slot.

Opened-and-refilled envelope (time-of-check/time-of-use, mutable/aliased archive): the has() witness is taken at receive time; the manifest write happens after. Examine whether the archive backing has() could change, be evicted, be re-added under the same key, or be aliased across concurrent landings between the witness and the durable write — an intact-looking seal that no longer witnesses the current interior. Also whether a long-lived Transport reused across sessions can carry a stale witness from a prior account.

Impression over empty clay (the reconciliation loop's own truthiness/shape edges as un-witnessed acceptance): walk the isinstance(source_artifacts, list) / isinstance(h, str) guards and the list-comprehension for any shape where an entry is treated as reconciled-or-absent rather than refused — a null/empty-list/non-list source_artifacts, a duplicate impression, a non-string element — such that a manifest with NO genuinely-witnessed root still lands (an envelope filed with no tokens, or the absence of an envelope silently read as 'nothing to witness' when a lineage root was in fact claimed elsewhere in the manifest, e.g. lineage vs source_artifacts).

Direct-witness (no-envelope) path preserved byte-for-byte (transport=None additive): construct the legacy receipt (no transport supplied) and confirm its control flow and side effects are the pre-diff path verbatim — the contributor path (source_artifacts built from real local bytes, sealed-over-tokens by construction) and every current caller enter on the scribe's direct witness with NO impression-check interposed. Any new guard, default, or evaluation-order change on the legacy account is a P1 regression even if the value entered is identical, because the §8.1 boundary and the contributor path ride that path.

Break-the-bulla-to-verify vs read-the-impression (does anything actually content-verify at THIS seam, or is it impressions all the way down): confirm the design's claim that the transfer 'owns' the content-break and this landing 'owns' the account-binding is actually true end-to-end — that somewhere a bulla is genuinely broken and tokens counted (bytes content-addressed) for the hash this gate relies on, not that the transfer records presence on the device's declared impression too, leaving NO layer that ever counts the tokens (two impression-checks composing, neither breaking clay).
severity_examples: P0: any path where an artifact_hash is ENTERED AS A TRUE CONTENT-COUNT (lands as a lineage root, redact/normalize proceeds) without a witnessed content-sealing behind it — a conforming Transport whose has() reports presence for a hash it never content-verified, so an impression pressed over empty clay is accepted; or the transfer layer ALSO trusting the device's declared impression, leaving no layer that ever breaks the bulla, so the whole chain is impressions with no token-count anywhere. This is a direct §8.1 lineage-root forgery: an unverified root entered as content-witnessed.

P1: cross-transaction bulla confusion — a genuine, correctly-content-verified raw sealed under session A accepted as session B's root because the session_id scoping the has() lookup is device-declared (sender names his own account) rather than the node's independently-owned account-number, so the wrong-session refusal the diff tests is bypassable by a sender who files a valid envelope under a foreign account. Also P1: any change to the transport=None direct-witness legacy path that alters when/whether it enters a receipt, even 'equivalently.'

P2: an opened-and-refilled TOCTOU/aliasing gap (archive state mutable between the has() witness and the durable write, or a long-lived Transport carrying a stale witness across sessions), or an impression-over-empty-clay shape edge (null/empty/non-list/duplicate source_artifacts, or a lineage root claimed in a manifest field the loop doesn't reconcile) that the schema permits but the sealing grammar should have refused — a receipt the shape-check lets pass but no witnessed sealing stands behind.
source_domain: Bronze-Age Mesopotamian sealed-bulla token accounting (pre-literate temple-storehouse provenance: shaped clay tokens sealed inside a hollow clay envelope whose exterior is cylinder-seal-impressed and counting-sign-marked; the impression is a PROMISE about the sealed interior trustworthy only because the seal was pressed over those tokens at intake; to VERIFY you must BREAK the bulla and count — a matching impression on an intact envelope proves someone once vouched for SOME contents, never that THESE contents are inside now; the three frauds are the empty-sealed impression, the genuine-envelope-misfiled-under-the-wrong-account, and the opened-and-refilled reseal)
success_hints: Read the transport.has() call in receive_device_manifest as the moment the accountant decides whether a present envelope's impression may be entered as a true count. The single highest-value finding is any way has()==true can hold WITHOUT a content-witnessed sealing having occurred — chase the guarantee into the Transport CONTRACT (does every conformer promise it?) rather than the InMemoryTransport double (which happens to content-address on send). A property proven only by the test double is an impression, not a broken bulla.

Separate the two authorities deliberately: the impression (artifact_hash string, device-authored, cheap to copy) versus the witnessed tokens (actual bytes content-addressed at intake). Then ask, at THIS seam, which one is actually consulted — if the node only ever compares impressions (has() on a device-declared hash, transfer trusting a device-declared hash) and never forces a token-count anywhere in the chain, the whole reconciliation certifies clay, not contents.

Trace session_id provenance to the has() key: is it the node's own derived account-number at the point of the lookup, or a value the device manifest declared and the sender controls? A sender who names his own session_id can file a legitimately-sealed envelope under any account — reproduce the diff's wrong-session test but with a device-CHOSEN session_id and see whether the binding still holds.

Prove the legacy no-envelope receipt is untouched: construct transport=None, diff the control flow and side-effect ordering against the pre-diff path, and confirm NO new guard/default/evaluation-order is interposed on the scribe's-direct-witness account — the concern is a changed WHEN/WHETHER of entry, not just an identical entered value.

Chase every non-raise resolution in the reconciliation loop (a source_artifacts that is null / empty-list / non-list / has duplicate or non-string entries, or a manifest that carries its lineage root in a field the loop never reconciles): each is a candidate 'enter a receipt with no witnessed tokens behind it.' The fail-closed claim holds only if EVERY such shape refuses rather than silently treating absence-of-envelope as nothing-to-witness.
task_context: Find any path where the source_artifacts reconciliation can be bypassed or tricked into accepting an unverified lineage root, where transport.has() being true does NOT actually imply content-verified bytes, where the (session_id, artifact_hash) keying can be confused across sessions, or where the additive transport=None path diverges from prior behavior. Verify the cross-language parity vector genuinely pins both production hashers (not a re-implementation) and can't pass vacuously. Rank by S8.1 lineage-integrity risk. Target: mk-lib S8.1 source_artifacts hash parity + fail-closed receive-time reconciliation (ingest.receive_device_manifest optional transport param reconciles every source_artifacts hash via transport.has(); cross-language parity vector + Python/Swift production-hasher tests; 491-line diff, docs/research/pr8-mk-lib-source-artifacts-hash-parity.diff).
